heading: INT. HARBOUR PILOT STATION - OFFICE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HARBOUR PILOT STATION - OFFICE - NIGHT
A cramped prefab office on stilts above a container yard.
Radar sweeps on a small green screen.
A kettle, three mugs, a corkboard of tide tables.
Rain on a tin roof.
DETECTIVE INSPECTOR RAKESH MALHOTRA (50s, creased raincoat, thorough rather than clever) sits on a plastic chair.
His notebook is open on his knee.
He has been here for two hours.
Opposite him, harbour pilot ANSELM DRUMMOND (50s, navy jersey, neat grey beard) fills the kettle from a bottle.
His hands are slow and exact.
At the desk, HARBOUR CLERK BIRGITTA STRAND (20s, headset, laminated lanyard) taps keys on a battered keyboard.
She is crying, but only in the way her throat works.
You said you didn't see the container.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: I said I didn't see it come off the ship.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: And you didn't see it sit on the quay.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: It sat on the quay all week. Everyone saw it.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: Birgitta?
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Container 4471. Customs hold on the fourteenth. Released on the sixteenth.
units.name: BIRGITTA

units.text: Who released it?
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: The system.
units.name: BIRGITTA

units.text: The system did that on its own?
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Somebody clicked something.
units.name: BIRGITTA

units.text: Drummond sets the kettle on its base and flicks the switch.
The element begins to tick.
He folds his arms and leans on the counter.
Inspector, I've been piloting ships into this harbour for twenty-six years. I bring in tankers the length of the high street through a channel two hundred feet wide. I do not click things.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: I'm not saying you did.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: You are saying something.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: Malhotra turns a page.
The paper rustles.
He reads a line to himself, then looks at the corkboard, where the tide table for the fifteenth has a pencil mark in the margin.
Whose handwriting is that?
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Mine.
units.name: BIRGITTA

units.text: Hers.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: Neither of you looked.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Birgitta swallows.
Drummond rubs his beard with the back of one hand.
The kettle starts to roar.
Steam beads on the window.
At 2:10 on the fifteenth, a pilot cutter left this station with one man aboard. The log says it went out for a routine inspection of a buoy.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: It did.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: The buoy has been missing since March.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Silence.
The kettle clicks off.
Nobody moves to pour.
It's my fault.
units.name: BIRGITTA

units.text: Birgitta.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: I released the hold. He told me it was paperwork. He said the owners would say thank you.
units.name: BIRGITTA

units.text: Who?
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: She presses her fingers hard against her mouth.
Drummond looks at her for a long time.
The ticking of the cooling kettle fills the room.
Then he sits, heavily, on the stool beside her, and takes her hand off the keyboard, and holds it in both of his.
It was me, Inspector.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: I thought it might be.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: She was frightened. I told her what to click.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: That's what she'll say in court, as well?
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: It's what happened.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: Malhotra closes the notebook.
Slides it into his coat.
Stands, bones popping.
He goes to the counter, takes the kettle, and pours three mugs of water over three bare teabags.
He sets the first before Birgitta, the second before Drummond, and holds the third himself.
Drink it while it's hot. The car's at the gate. It'll wait.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: DRUMMOND

units.text: Don't thank me yet.
units.name: MALHOTRA

units.text: Drummond lifts the mug.
His hands shake for the first time.
A little tea spills onto the tide table, spreading across the pencil mark in a brown stain.
Birgitta lays her head on his shoulder.
Outside, a ship's horn sounds, long and low, from beyond the breakwater.
It is the sound of something coming home.
FADE OUT.
